title: Running and Inspecting Your First Workflow knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Running and Inspecting Your First Workflow?
options: Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
The Actions tab exposes each workflow run, its job graph, step logs, statuses, duration, and retry controls for diagnosing behavior.
questions.answer_key: The Actions tab exposes each workflow run, its job graph, step logs, statuses, duration, and retry controls for diagnosing behavior.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of running and inspecting your first workflow: The Actions tab exposes each workflow run, its job graph, step logs, statuses, duration, and retry controls for diagnosing behavior. questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to running and inspecting your first workflow?
options: Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: The Actions tab exposes each workflow run, its job graph, step logs, statuses, duration, and retry controls for diagnosing behavior. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
